neighbours.label: concessive / parenthetical discourse markers that qualify the previous clause (however, of course, though, 'not that')
fire: She did win the race in the end; the weather, however, was miserable.
They never admitted it, of course, but everyone knew who had taken the cake.
The house was small, though nobody in the family ever complained.
He visited the shop every week, not that he ever bought anything.
The plan, however, depended entirely on the bank agreeing to lend.
I'd seen the film before, of course, so the ending was no surprise.
It rained all afternoon; we went for the walk anyway, though.
My brother called again last night, not that I picked up.
quiet: She did win the race in the end, and the weather was miserable.
They admitted it at once, and everyone knew who had taken the cake.
The house was small, and everyone in the family was very happy there.
He visited the shop every week and bought a loaf of bread each time.
The plan depended entirely on the bank agreeing to lend.
I'd seen the film twice before, so the ending was no surprise.
It rained all afternoon, so we went for the walk the next day.
My brother called again last night, and we talked for an hour.

notes: Card top examples: ' that' in 'not that', ' however', ' course' in 'of course', ' though', also Korean 물론 ('of course'). The - pole holds the other side: 'despite', 'not all', 'not alone'. Near misses keep the narrative without a concessive marker.
